scenes.narration: Neural networks learn by adjusting weights to reduce prediction errors.
scenes.heading: How Neural Networks Learn

scenes.narration: A forward pass moves inputs through layers of neurons. Each neuron applies an activation function after summing weighted inputs.
Activation functions add non-linearity so the network models complex patterns. Without them, the network acts like a linear model.

params.text: Activation functions add non-linearity; without them the network acts linear.

scenes.narration: A loss function compares the output to the correct answer. It measures how far the prediction is from the target.
Backpropagation uses the chain rule to send error gradients backward. It computes gradients for every weight efficiently, layer by layer.
An optimizer updates weights using gradients and a learning rate.
This cycle repeats thousands of times.

params.text: Training cycles repeat thousands of times to minimize loss.

facts.text: Backpropagation applies the chain rule efficiently by propagating derivatives backward, one layer at a time, from the output layer to the input layer, avoiding redundant calculations.
facts.quote: It is an efficient application of the chain rule to neural networks. Backpropagation efficiently computes the gradient of the loss with respect to the network weights for a single input–output example. It does this by propagating derivatives backward, one layer at a time, from the output layer to the input layer, thereby avoiding redundant chain-rule calculations.

facts.text: The chain rule is used to compute the gradient of the loss with respect to each weight in a neural network during training.
facts.quote: It is an efficient application of the chain rule to neural networks.

facts.text: Standard back-propagation locks each layer during training, causing most of the network to stay idle while waiting for parameter updates.
facts.quote: New training iteration can only start after all the parameters in the network are updated. Thus, each layer of the network is locked until their dependent parameters have been computed.

facts.text: Re-computation during training introduces a difference between weights used in the first forward pass and those used in the second forward pass, leading to stale gradients and potential performance loss.
facts.quote: The adoption of re-computation causes a difference between weights of modules used in the second FP during the backward stage and that used in the first FP during the forward stage for the same batch of data.

facts.text: The training process requires a learning rate (η) and a gradient shrinking factor (β) as required parameters.
facts.quote: Required: Learning rate η, gradient shrinking factor β.

facts.text: AlexNet's success in 2012 depended on large datasets, GPU computing, and improved training methods.
facts.quote: AlexNet's success in 2012 was enabled by the convergence of three developments that had matured over the previous decade: large-scale labeled datasets, general-purpose GPU computing, and improved training methods for deep neural networks.

facts.text: AlexNet won the ImageNet competition with a top-5 error rate of 15.3%, beating the runner-up by over 10.8 percentage points.
facts.quote: The network achieved a top-5 error rate of 15.3% to win the contest, more than 10.8% points better than the runner-up.
